judgements.concept: Python for ML ecosystem (NumPy, pandas, matplotlib, scikit-learn API)
judgements.why: Learner knows Python but not ML libraries; this is the essential starting point for everything else.

judgements.concept: Supervised learning framing (classification vs regression)
judgements.why: Core mental model — without this, no model selection or evaluation makes sense.

judgements.concept: Unsupervised learning framing (clustering, dimensionality reduction)
judgements.why: Production ML is overwhelmingly supervised; unsupervised can be deferred.

judgements.concept: Train/validation/test split & cross-validation
judgements.why: Non-negotiable for any credible model evaluation; directly enables production reliability.

judgements.concept: Model evaluation metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, RMSE, MAE)
judgements.why: Must choose the right metric for the business problem; production models live/die by this.

judgements.concept: Feature preprocessing (scaling, encoding, missing values, datetime, text)
judgements.why: Real data is messy; preprocessing is where most production failures originate.

judgements.concept: Feature engineering (interactions, polynomials, domain-specific, embeddings)
judgements.why: Important but open-ended; one weekend cannot cover domain-specific engineering meaningfully.

judgements.concept: Linear models (logistic/linear regression with regularization)
judgements.why: Baseline models that are interpretable, fast, and often sufficient; essential first algorithm.

judgements.concept: Tree-based models (decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting)
judgements.why: Industry standard for tabular data; random forest gives strong baseline with minimal tuning.

judgements.concept: Gradient boosting libraries (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost)
judgements.why: State-of-the-art for structured data; CatBoost handles categoricals natively — high leverage for weekend learner.

judgements.concept: Neural network fundamentals (MLP, backprop, activation functions)
judgements.why: Too deep for one weekend with zero ML background; tabular production ML rarely starts here.

judgements.concept: Deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow/Keras)
judgements.why: Not needed for tabular production models; adds complexity without payoff in this timeframe.

judgements.concept: Hyperparameter tuning (grid search, random search, Bayesian optimization)
judgements.why: Random search + cross-validation is learnable in hours and dramatically improves results.

judgements.concept: Model selection & comparison
judgements.why: Must compare 2-3 model families quickly; the practical skill is knowing what to try and when to stop.

judgements.concept: Overfitting/underfitting diagnosis & regularization
judgements.why: Core diagnostic skill; without it, models fail silently in production.

judgements.concept: Imbalanced data handling (resampling, class weights, threshold tuning)
judgements.why: Real production data is almost always imbalanced; threshold tuning is a high-ROI technique.

judgements.concept: Pipeline construction (sklearn Pipeline, ColumnTransformer)
judgements.why: The single most important production pattern — prevents train/serve skew and enables deployment.

judgements.concept: Experiment tracking (MLflow, Weights & Biases, ClearML)
judgements.why: Lightweight tracking (even just MLflow local) teaches reproducibility; can be learned in 30 minutes.

judgements.concept: Model serialization & versioning (joblib, ONNX, model registry)
judgements.why: joblib/ONNX export is the bridge to serving; model registry concept is essential mental model.

judgements.concept: Model serving patterns (REST API, batch inference, streaming, edge)
judgements.why: Must understand the deployment target; REST + batch covers 90% of cases.

judgements.concept: API frameworks for ML (FastAPI, Flask, Triton, TorchServe)
judgements.why: FastAPI is Pythonic, fast, and teaches the serving pattern in one file.

judgements.concept: Containerization for ML (Docker, multi-stage builds, GPU images)
judgements.why: Docker is the universal deployment artifact; a minimal Dockerfile is teachable in 20 minutes.

judgements.concept: Orchestration & scheduling (Airflow, Prefect, Dagster, cron)
judgements.why: Orchestration is infrastructure, not model building; cron or a simple script suffices for weekend scope.

judgements.concept: Data validation & schema enforcement (Great Expectations, pandera, TFDV)
judgements.why: pandera/sklearn's validation can be shown in 15 minutes; prevents silent data drift failures.

judgements.concept: Monitoring: data drift, concept drift, model performance
judgements.why: Operational concern for running systems; learner isn't deploying to production traffic yet.

judgements.concept: Automated retraining & CI/CD for ML (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins)
judgements.why: Full CI/CD is a team/infra concern; out of scope for individual weekend learning.

judgements.concept: A/B testing & canary deployments for models
judgements.why: Requires production traffic and infrastructure; not a model-building skill.

judgements.concept: Feature stores (Feast, Tecton, Hopsworks)
judgements.why: Organizational infrastructure; overkill for individual practitioner weekend.

judgements.concept: Model optimization (quantization, distillation, ONNX Runtime, TensorRT)
judgements.why: Optimization comes after a working model; premature for this learner.

judgements.concept: Distributed training & scaling (DDP, FSDP, Ray, Horovod)
judgements.why: Irrelevant for tabular data sizes typical of weekend projects.

judgements.concept: Transfer learning & fine-tuning (vision, NLP, tabular)
judgements.why: Requires deep learning foundation; not applicable to tabular production ML.

judgements.concept: Responsible ML (fairness, interpretability, SHAP, LIME, privacy)
judgements.why: SHAP for tree models is fast to learn and essential for stakeholder trust in production.

sequence: Production ML End-to-End: From Data to Deployed Model
output.why: Single weekend capacity with zero ML background demands one contiguous learning arc — every concept builds toward the same deployed model artifact; splitting would fracture the end-to-end mental model the learner must internalize in 48 hours.

exclusions.consequence: Cannot discover structure in unlabeled data or reduce feature dimensionality for visualization/compression; production systems occasionally need this for anomaly detection or preprocessing.
exclusions.when_to_learn: When a project requires pattern discovery without labels or when feature count explodes and supervised feature selection isn't enough.

exclusions.consequence: Model performance plateaus at baseline; cannot create predictive signals that require domain knowledge or non-linear combinations.
exclusions.when_to_learn: After first model baseline is established and metrics show headroom — typically week 2 of a real project.

exclusions.topic: Neural network fundamentals (MLP, backprop, activation functions)
exclusions.consequence: Cannot build or debug deep models; tabular production ML rarely needs this, but vision/NLP tasks are inaccessible.
exclusions.when_to_learn: When the problem domain shifts to images, text, or audio — or when tabular gradients demand representation learning.

exclusions.consequence: Cannot implement custom architectures, use transfer learning, or leverage GPU acceleration for large-scale deep models.
exclusions.when_to_learn: Concurrently with neural network fundamentals, when the first deep learning project starts.

exclusions.consequence: Retraining pipelines run manually or via brittle cron; no visibility into DAG failures, retries, or backfills.
exclusions.when_to_learn: When model retraining frequency exceeds weekly or when multiple interdependent pipelines exist.

exclusions.topic: Monitoring: data drift, concept drift, model performance
exclusions.consequence: Silent degradation in production — predictions worsen without alerts; business impact discovered late.
exclusions.when_to_learn: Before first model serves live traffic; implement alongside serving layer.

exclusions.topic: Automated retraining & CI/CD for ML (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins)
exclusions.consequence: Model updates require manual intervention; no automated testing of model artifacts; deployment risk scales with frequency.
exclusions.when_to_learn: When team owns multiple models or retraining cadence is daily/weekly.

exclusions.topic: A/B testing & canary deployments for models
exclusions.consequence: Cannot safely compare model versions in production; full cutover risks user-facing regressions.
exclusions.when_to_learn: When model serves user-facing decisions and traffic volume supports statistical comparison.

exclusions.consequence: Feature definitions drift between training and serving; duplicate engineering across models; no point-in-time correctness.
exclusions.when_to_learn: When 3+ models share features or when feature freshness becomes a correctness requirement.

exclusions.topic: Model optimization (quantization, distillation, ONNX Runtime, TensorRT)
exclusions.consequence: Inference latency/cost stays high; edge deployment impossible; GPU utilization suboptimal.
exclusions.when_to_learn: After model accuracy is validated and latency/cost become production constraints.

exclusions.topic: Distributed training & scaling (DDP, FSDP, Ray, Horovod)
exclusions.consequence: Training time scales linearly with data/model size; cannot train large deep models or process TB-scale tabular data.
exclusions.when_to_learn: When single-GPU training exceeds 24 hours or model/data exceed GPU memory.

exclusions.consequence: Cannot leverage pretrained foundations for vision/NLP; tabular transfer learning remains niche and less impactful.
exclusions.when_to_learn: When starting a vision/NLP project with limited labeled data — or when tabular pretrained models mature.

modules.capability: Design, train, evaluate, and deploy a production-ready ML model end-to-end: frame a business problem as supervised learning, build a preprocessing+model pipeline with ColumnTransformer, compare linear/tree/boosting baselines with cross-validation, diagnose overfitting and handle imbalance, serialize the pipeline to joblib/ONNX, wrap it in a FastAPI service with Pydantic validation, containerize it with a multi-stage Dockerfile, and log experiments in MLflow — all on a real tabular dataset.
